questions.question: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two points on the ground at distances 'a' and 'b' (where a > b) from the base of the tower and in the same straight line are complementary. What is the height of the tower?
questions.explanation: Let height be h. Angle 1 is theta, angle 2 is (90 - theta). tan theta = h / a. tan(90 - theta) = cot theta = h / b. Multiplying: tan theta * cot theta = (h/a) * (h/b) => 1 = h^2 / (ab) => h^2 = ab => h = sqrt(ab).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 9, Exercise 9.1 Question 16

questions.subtopic: Poles on Road Equal Height Solution
questions.question: Two poles of equal heights stand on either side of an 80 m wide road. From a point between them on the road, the angles of elevation of the tops are 60 degrees and 30 degrees. Find the height of the poles and the distances of the point from the poles.
options: Height = 40 m, distances = 40 m and 40 m
Height = 20 m, distances = 30 m and 50 m
Height = 20 sqrt(3) m, distances = 20 m and 60 m
Height = 30 sqrt(3) m, distances = 25 m and 55 m
questions.explanation: Let point be at distance x from pole 1 and (80 - x) from pole 2. h = x * tan 60 deg = x*sqrt(3). Also h = (80 - x) * tan 30 deg = (80 - x)/sqrt(3). Equating: x*sqrt(3) = (80 - x)/sqrt(3) => 3x = 80 - x => 4x = 80 => x = 20 m. Distances are 20 m and 60 m. Height h = 20*sqrt(3) m.

questions.question: A straight highway leads to the foot of a tower. A man standing at the top observes a car at an angle of depression of 30 degrees, which is approaching the foot of the tower with uniform speed. Six seconds later, the angle of depression of the car is found to be 60 degrees. Find the time taken by the car to reach the foot of the tower from this point.
questions.explanation: Let tower height be h. At 60 deg, distance x = h / tan 60 = h/sqrt(3). At 30 deg, distance y = h / tan 30 = h*sqrt(3) = 3x. Distance traveled in 6 s = y - x = 3x - x = 2x. Speed = 2x / 6 = x / 3 per second. Remaining distance to foot is x. Time required = x / (x/3) = 3 seconds.

questions.question: If the angle of elevation of a cloud from a point 'h' metres above a lake is alpha and the angle of depression of its reflection in the lake is beta, what is the height of the cloud above the lake surface?
options: h (tan beta - tan alpha) / (tan beta + tan alpha)
h (tan beta + tan alpha) / (tan beta - tan alpha)
questions.explanation: Let height of cloud above lake be H. Cloud is H - h above observation point; its reflection is H + h below observation point. Horizontal distance d = (H - h)/tan alpha = (H + h)/tan beta. (H - h) tan beta = (H + h) tan alpha => H(tan beta - tan alpha) = h(tan beta + tan alpha) => H = h(tan beta + tan alpha) / (tan beta - tan alpha).

questions.subtopic: Bird on Top of Tree Flight Speed
questions.question: A bird is sitting on top of an 80 m tall tree. From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the bird is 45 degrees. The bird flies away horizontally at a constant height. After 2 seconds, the angle of elevation from the same point is 30 degrees. Find the speed of flight of the bird. (Use sqrt(3) = 1.732)
questions.explanation: Initial ground distance d1 = 80 / tan 45 = 80 m. After 2 s, d2 = 80 / tan 30 = 80*sqrt(3) m. Distance flown = d2 - d1 = 80(sqrt(3) - 1) = 80(0.732) = 58.56 m. Speed = Distance / Time = 58.56 / 2 = 29.28 m/s.

questions.question: A round balloon of radius 'r' subtends an angle alpha at the eye of the observer, while the angle of elevation of its centre is beta. What is the height of the centre of the balloon from the ground?
questions.explanation: Let centre of balloon be C and observer be O. The angle subtended by the balloon is alpha, so the half angle between line of sight to centre and tangent is alpha/2. In right triangle formed by tangent: sin(alpha/2) = r / OC => OC = r / sin(alpha/2) = r cosec(alpha/2). In right triangle for height of centre: sin beta = Height / OC => Height = OC * sin beta = r sin beta cosec(alpha/2).
